title: Private Deployments - VPC & On-Prem Combined Reference (Deployment, Day-2, Upgrades, Packaging, Customer Requirements)
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Summary:
This combined reference consolidates best-practice guidance for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers reference architectures, on-prem packaging requirements, network and security configuration, day-2 operations, upgrade and rollback procedures, and a customer requirements library to accelerate sales-to-deploy handoffs. Use this as the canonical deployment playbook for customer engagements that require Private (VPC or on-prem) installations.

Scope:
- Environments: VPC-connected Private control plane, air-gapped on-prem packaging.
- Components included: Control plane components, inference runtime, model store, metrics & logs collectors, KMS/HSM integrations, ingress/egress guards.
- Audience: Platform engineers (owner), solutions engineering, SRE, security reviewers, professional services.

Owners & Contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-private-deployments (platform)
- Runbook on-call: SRE team (pager roster)
- Escalation: Lead PM (Priya Shah) -> Head of Platform (Mateo Garcia)

SLOs & Operational Targets:
- Control plane API availability: 99.95% monthly
- Inference latency (p95 token): <= 150ms for realtime tiers (depends on customer hardware)
- Model upload/manifest operations: p99 < 30s
- Alerting: Pager on control plane API error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes

Reference architectures (high level):
1) VPC-hosted private control plane + customer VPC inference nodes
   - Components: managed control plane in Redwood region, customer VPC peered or PrivateLink, inference nodes in customer subnet (ASG/VMSS), NAT for outbound updates optional, VPC endpoints for S3-compatible model store.
   - Network diagram: control-plane -> PrivateLink -> customer VPC: load-balancer -> inference nodes -> KMS/HSM -> logging/monitoring agent -> outbound model registry pull.

2) Fully on-prem (air-gapped)
   - Components: on-prem control plane bundle (OCI/tar), local model registry, on-prem KMS/HSM, local observability stack (Prometheus + Grafana), optional HA via private load-balancer and three control-plane replicas.

3) Hybrid: Customer-managed control plane (VPC) with Redwood-managed fallback control-plane for emergency failover.

Network & Security (VPC guidance):
- Required CIDR blocks: reserve /22 for inference pool (adjust to GPU count).
- Subnet layout: public (bastion/nginx), private (inference), management (KMS/HSM, DBs).
- Security groups: restrict inference nodes to control-plane and monitoring CIDRs. SSH access via bastion only.
- IAM & KMS: prefer customer-managed KMS with key rotation policies. Provide an IAM role with least privilege for model pull and metrics export.
- Egress controls: restrict outbound to Redwood IP ranges or model registry endpoints; use proxy for telemetry when requested.

On-Prem Packaging & Prerequisites:
- Supported OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (x86_64) and select RHEL 8 builds documented in packaging README.
- Container runtime: Docker 24.x or containerd; Kubernetes supported versions: 1.24-1.27 (see compatibility matrix).
- Hardware: GPU recommendations: NVIDIA A10/A100 or AMD MI250; minimum 16GB GPU memory for smaller models, 80GB+ for large-llama-class models.
- Storage: fast NVMe for local cache (recommended >= 1TB), network filesystem for model archives (if used).
- Packaging artifacts: systemd unit + container images + helm charts (for k8s). Use provided packaging script to produce an airgap tarball.

Packaging Example (airgap preparation):
1) On a host with internet: ./packaging/create-airgap-bundle.sh --version 2027.02 --output redwood-airgap-2027-02.tar.gz
2) Verify checksum: sha256sum redwood-airgap-2027-02.tar.gz
3) Transfer to customer site via approved media.

Day-2 Operations (routine):
- Health checks: run ./tools/check-health.sh (returns JSON with component status).
- Model management: upload via local registry API or S3-compatible endpoint. Recommended model retention policy: keep N most-used models (N configurable; default 10).
- Scaling: In k8s, scale inference deployment via HPA based on custom metric (inflight-requests-per-GPU). For VMs, use autoscaling group policies: target CPU 70% or GPU-utilization 60%.
- Backups: etcd/db snapshots daily, object-store replication for model artifacts. Verify backups weekly.
- Patch windows: schedule monthly with one-week maintenance window; follow upgrade guide below.

Upgrade & Rollback Procedures (control plane and runtime):
- Pre-upgrade checklist:
  1. Verify backups exist and are tested (etcd snapshot + model store snapshot).
  2. Confirm canary cluster or staging environment mirrors production.
  3. Freeze model uploads and non-critical config changes.
  4. Notify stakeholders and users with scheduled window.

- Control plane upgrade (k8s helm example):
  1. helm repo update redwood-inference && helm fetch redwood-inference/control-plane --version 2027.02.
  2. helm upgrade control-plane redwood-inference/control-plane -f values-prod.yaml --wait --timeout 15m
  3. Validate pods: kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide && kubectl rollout status deployment/control-plane -n redwood
  4. Smoke tests: ./tools/smoke-control-plane.sh --endpoint https://controlplane.customer.local

- Runtime (inference) upgrade can be done using progressive canary:
  1. Add new nodepool with upgraded runtime image.
  2. Route 5% traffic to new nodes; monitor latency and error rates for 30 minutes.
  3. If metrics stable, increase to 25% then 50%.
  4. Full cutover.

- Rollback steps (if failure detected):
  - For helm-based control plane: helm rollback control-plane <prevRelease> --wait
  - For runtime nodes: remove upgraded nodepool and re-add previous nodepool; redirect traffic accordingly.
  - Post-rollback: run full consistency checks and replay any failed model uploads from snapshot.

Incident Playbook (high level):
1. Detection: Alert on control plane error rate or inference p95 regression.
2. Triage: SRE runbook: capture logs (kubectl logs), collect metrics snapshot, run ./tools/collect-diagnostics.sh.
3. Mitigation: Route traffic to fallback model variant or lower-latency tier. If systemic, scale up healthy capacity.
4. Postmortem: Create incident page, assign severity, perform RCA within 72 hours.

Customer Requirements Library (minimums for engagement):
- Network: Dedicated VPC or VLAN with /22 reservation or explicit capacity plan; firewall rules to allow control-plane endpoints and monitoring exports.
- Identity: Customer-managed KMS recommended; service account or IAM role with least-privilege policy (list provided below).
- Hardware: GPU type and quantity; NIC speed (>= 25Gb recommended for high-throughput workloads).
- Observability: Agent install (prometheus node exporter + filebeat) required, or agree to use Redwood-managed telemetry with approved outbound access.
- Compliance: If regulated, provide SOC2 report and enable audit-logging; for air-gapped, Redwood provides offline attestation bundle.

Minimum IAM policy (example, trim for customer's provider):
- s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject on model-bucket
- kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt on customer-managed-key
- ec2:DescribeInstances (read-only for autoscaling)

Checklists (deployment day):
- Pre-deploy: verify network connectivity, KMS handshake, DNS entries created, and firewall rules in place.
- Deploy: apply infra (Terraform/Ansible) -> deploy control plane -> deploy runtime -> run smoke tests.
- Post-deploy: enable monitoring dashboards, set alert thresholds, handoff runbook to customer ops.

Appendix: Example Terraform snippet (VPC endpoint):
```
resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_models" {
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  service_name = "com.amazonaws.us-west-2.s3"
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Gateway"
  route_table_ids = var.route_table_ids
}
```

Appendix: Example systemd unit (inference runtime container):
```
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Inference Runtime
After=docker.service

[Service]
Restart=always
TimeoutStartSec=0
ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker run --rm --gpus all --name rwd-runtime \n  -v /var/lib/redwood:/var/lib/redwood \n  -p 8080:8080 redwood/runtime:2027.02

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```
